1) The partition function of a quantum statistical system in thermal equilibrium at a temperature T is given by the integral over field eigenvalues (boundary fields) at a fixed temperature of the density matrix at the temperature in the Schroedinger functional representation.

the effective action of thermal field theories can be expressed in terms of a classical field, {phi}{sub C}, which is a functional of boundary fields; the effective action is the same as the zero-temperature effective action, if we trade free-field propagators at zero-temperature for their finite temperature counterparts; the two-point correlation function of the classical field can be expressed as a function of the two-point correlation of the boundary field.

(1) the one-loop effective potential of a scalar field at finite temperature has the same expression as at zero-temperature, if written in terms a certain classical field, and if we use free propagators at finite temperature instead of zero temperature; and (2) the one-loop finite-temperature two-point correlation function can be expressed in terms of the two-point correlation function at zero temperature.
